title: Standard refinement of an arbitrary prime-to-ell alteration cover
statement: Let $S$ be an integral Noetherian scheme [def-pc-integral-scheme, def-pc-scheme, def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], where Noetherian means admitting a finite affine cover by spectra of Noetherian rings, with every affine coordinate ring quasi-excellent [def-exc-excellent-ring]. Let $\ell$ be a prime invertible on $S$. Let $(q_b:T_b\to S)_{b\in B}$ be a finite covering family in $\operatorname{alt}/S$ for the topology of $\ell'$-alterations [def-per-prime-to-ell-alteration-topology]. There exist an integral Noetherian scheme $S'$, a proper morphism $p:S'\to S$ which is an isomorphism over a dense open of $S$, a finite family of separated etale morphisms $e_i:E_i\to S'$, and finite locally free surjective [def-weil-surjective-morphism] morphisms $a_i:W_i\to E_i$ of constant positive ranks $r_i$ prime to $\ell$. All $E_i,W_i$ are integral Noetherian schemes and $S',E_i,W_i$ are of finite type over $S$; the $e_i$ are of finite type. The family $(e_i)_i$ is completely decomposed, meaning that for each $s'\in S'$ there are $i$ and $z\in E_i$ above $s'$ for which $\kappa(s')\to\kappa(z)$ is an isomorphism [def-weil-residue-field]. For each $i$ there are $b(i)\in B$ and an $S$-morphism $h_i:W_i\to T_{b(i)}$ with $q_{b(i)}h_i=pe_ia_i$. Proper and separated use [def-weil-proper-morphism], etale uses [def-weil-etale-morphism], finite type uses [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], and finite locally free uses [def-pc-finite-locally-free]; the latter means finite, flat and locally of finite presentation, with the specified rank measured by fibre dimension.

source.place: Expose II, Theorem 3.2.3, printed pp. 30--31, with finite-cover Corollary 2.2.4, printed p. 27; finite form as used in Expose XIII 3.2.1, printed p. 199. On the integral Noetherian sources the finite flat maps have positive constant finite locally free rank; etale sources may be refined by affine opens.

proof.text: Apply [lem-per-alteration-cover-proper-normal-form] with $X=S$ and the given finite covering family. Its hypotheses are exactly the integral, Noetherian, quasi-excellent and invertible-prime hypotheses here. Obtain $f:Y\to S$ proper surjective with $Y$ integral, $d=[k(Y):k(S)]>0$ prime to $\ell$, a finite completely decomposed separated etale family $v_t:V_t\to Y$, and maps $V_t\to T_{b(t)}$ over $S$.

source.place: II Theorem 3.2.1; first input to II Theorem 3.2.3.

proof.text: Apply [lem-per-integral-etale-chart-flatification] to the single chart $S\xrightarrow{1}S$ and $Y\to S$. This gives a proper dense-open isomorphism $p_0:S_0\to S$ with $S_0$ normal integral Noetherian, and an integral $Y_0$ mapping to $Y$, finite locally free surjective of rank $d$ over $S_0$. Pull back each $V_t\to Y$ along $Y_0\to Y$, obtaining $V_t^0\to Y_0$. These maps are etale by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-covering-base-change]; separatedness and finite type are stable under base change by the cited permanence statement. The pulled-back family is completely decomposed: for $y_0\mapsto y$, a lift with residue field $\kappa(y)$ gives after tensoring with $\kappa(y_0)$ a rational point above $y_0$. The projections $V_t^0\to V_t$ retain all maps to $T_{b(t)}$.

source.place: II Theorem 3.2.3, platification reduction; base change of a completely decomposed family.

proof.text: Apply [lem-per-finite-flat-cd-etale-exchange] to $Y_0\to S_0$ and $(V_t^0\to Y_0)_t$. The finite locally free rank is the same $d$ as in Step 1, hence positive and prime to $\ell$. Obtain a finite completely decomposed family $u_j:U_j\to S_0$, finite locally free surjections $Z_j\to U_j$ of positive ranks $d_j$ prime to $\ell$, and maps $Z_j\to V_{t(j)}^0\to T_{b(t(j))}$ over $S$. The $U_j,Z_j$ are Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian]. Split each $U_j$ into its finitely many normal integral open-and-closed components using [lem-fin-etale-normal-components], and restrict $Z_j$ and its map accordingly. Ranks are unchanged by this restriction, and every residue-field lift remains in one component, so the enlarged finite family is still completely decomposed. Discard empty charts.

source.place: II Theorem 3.2.3, exchange assertion and integral etale charts.

proof.text: For each integral chart $U_j$ write $K=k(U_j)$ and let $B$ be the finite-dimensional generic fibre algebra of $Z_j\to U_j$, of dimension $d_j$. Construct a composition series of $B$ as a $B$-module by repeatedly choosing a proper submodule of largest $K$-dimension; dimensions decrease, so it terminates. Each simple quotient is $B/\mathfrak m$ for a maximal ideal: any nonzero vector generates it and its annihilator is maximal. Additivity of vector-space dimension gives $d_j=\sum_a[B/\mathfrak m_a:K]$. Since $\ell\nmid d_j$, one summand has degree $n_j$ prime to $\ell$. Take the closure of this generic-fibre point in $Z_j$ with its reduced induced structure, supplied by [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-induced-closed-subscheme], and call it $F_j$. It is integral: its space is the closure of a point, hence irreducible, and its scheme structure is reduced. Its generic field is $B/\mathfrak m_a$. The map $F_j\to U_j$ is finite by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-finite] and [lem-weil-pbc-finite-composition], hence proper by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-proper]. Its image is closed and contains the generic point of $U_j$, so it is surjective. It maps to the same $T_{b(t(j))}$ as $Z_j$. No flatness of $F_j\to U_j$ is claimed at this stage.

source.place: II Theorem 3.2.3, integral sources: select a prime-to-ell generic component before the final platification; the dimension argument is written out.

proof.text: The scheme $S_0$ is quasi-excellent by [lem-per-quasi-excellent-finite-type-stability], since it is of finite type over $S$. Apply [lem-per-integral-etale-chart-flatification] simultaneously to the finite family $U_j\to S_0$ and the integral proper dominant maps $F_j\to U_j$ from Step 4. All generic degrees are the positive integers $n_j$ prime to $\ell$. It gives $b:S'\to S_0$ proper and an isomorphism over a dense open, integral Noetherian $E_j=U_j\times_{S_0}S'$, and integral Noetherian $W_j$ mapping to $F_j$, finite locally free surjective of rank $n_j$ over $E_j$. Set $p=p_0b$; it is proper by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-composition]. Its dense-open isomorphism follows by intersecting the isomorphism open for $b$ with the inverse image of that for $p_0$, and identifying this intersection with its open image in $S$ under $p_0$. Both opens contain the generic point. The maps $e_j:E_j\to S'$ are separated etale of finite type by base-change permanence, and completely decomposed by the same rational-point tensor calculation as in Step 2. Compose $W_j\to F_j\to Z_j\to V_{t(j)}^0\to T_{b(t(j))}$ to define $h_j$. Every arrow is over $S$, so $q_{b(t(j))}h_j=pe_ja_j$. The two flatification conclusions give finite type of $S_0$ over $S$ and of $S',E_j,W_j$ over $S_0$; composing with $p_0$ gives finite type over $S$ by [lem-sfb-finite-type-composition-base-change] (1), and $E_j,W_j,S'$ are Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian]. The indexing family is finite. These are all clauses of the item.
